title: DARE: Difficulty Analysis for Repair Enhancement
abstract: arXiv:2611.05797v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: LLM-based coding agents are primarily evaluated by their solve rates. However, this metric does not reveal how difficult the solved tasks are or account for differences intask difficulty across benchmarks. Determining the difficulty of individual tasks by repeatedly running multiple agents is costly, while a predicted difficulty score alone provides limited guidance on what support an agent needs. To address these challenges, we propose DARE (Difficulty Analysis for Repair Enhancement), which integrates repair-task difficulty measurement, prediction, feature-group contribution analysis, and task-specific repair support. We define continuous task difficulty as the observed failure rate across multiple coding agents. The DARE difficulty model predicts this difficulty using 151 static features extracted from benchmark artifacts. translated_title: DARE：面向修复增强的难度分析
translated_abstract: 基于大语言模型（LLM）的编程智能体主要通过解决率来进行评估。然而，这一指标既无法揭示已解决任务的难度，也无法考虑不同基准测试之间任务难度的差异。通过重复运行多个智能体来确定单个任务的难度成本高昂，而仅凭预测的难度分数对智能体需要何种支持提供的指导也十分有限。为了应对这些挑战，我们提出了DARE（Difficulty Analysis for Repair Enhancement，面向修复增强的难度分析），该框架集成了修复任务难度测量、预测、特征组贡献分析以及任务特定的修复支持。我们将连续的任务难度定义为跨多个编程智能体观察到的失败率。DARE难度模型利用从基准测试产物中提取的151个静态特征来预测这一难度。该框架还分析了七个修复任务特征组的贡献，以识别特征……
tldr: 提出DARE框架，利用从基准测试产物中提取的151个静态特征预测编程修复任务的难度（定义为多个智能体的观察失败率），并结合七个特征组的贡献分析，为编程智能体提供任务特定的修复支持。
en_tdlr: DARE is a framework that predicts the difficulty of program repair tasks (defined as the observed failure rate across multiple coding agents) using 151 static features extracted from benchmark artifacts, and leverages feature-group contribution analysis to provide task-specific repair support for LLM-based coding agents.
